launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-code
description: Cloud Code — our own signed build of Acode (the Android code editor), vendored at ac_cloud-code/ as owned code (#562), with a 7-tab bottom nav over it: Backlog | Editor | Repos | Chat | Agents | Browser | MyTerminal. Acode is the UPSTREAM PROJECT, never the product name. The Editor tab is Acode untouched; the other six live in src/cloud/ behind one seam in src/main.js. See CLOUD-CODE.md.
_doc_vendored_engine: Byte-identical to ac_cloud-code/build.sh, enforced by cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh parity check so the shipped engine and the vendored copy cannot drift.
_doc_name: #562 asked for ac_cloud-ide-acode. Not used: #561 retired the cloud-ide brand, and test-app-names-pattern.sh T9 fails any build.json value matching cloud[-_ ]?ide as a whole word, which 'cloud-ide-acode' does. cloud-code is canonical cloud-{name} (#351), collides with no fleet id, and names the function, not the upstream.

android._doc_application_id: The install identity, set by build-extras.gradle in onVariants. Cordova's widget id (config.xml) stays com.foxdebug.acode because it is also the Java namespace that upstream plugin sources import R from; only the applicationId moves. A new id, so it installs NEXT TO an upstream Acode rather than over it (and the one provider authority upstream hardcoded is now ${applicationId}-scoped for the same reason).
android._doc_version: version_name follows Acode's own package.json version at the pinned revision. version_code was 1 for the first published APK (run 36119903627, sha 56f57e334), 2 from #562 publish, 3 from #599 (Home Configs permissions icon + Repos root picker), 4 from #743 (fleet mesh membership via libs:core), 5 from the Chat tab (Home replaced: agents, the shared model catalogue, the CloudChat plugin), and 6 from every fleet agent (OpenClaw, live /health.modes) and the full-page Model picker (A0-A3, per agent), 7 from the DeepSeek harness, 8 from reading the shared agents.json, 9 from the fleet's shared navigation bars (#1158); it must be bumped again for the fleet updater to offer a rebuild (it only offers strictly newer codes).
android._doc_target_sdk: Not ours to set: Acode's hooks/post-process.js pins targetSdk 28 for the F-Droid flavour (legacy storage + exec), which is the flavour built here. Recorded so the number is visible, not restated in gradle.
android._doc_no_gradle_module: No gradle_module is declared on purpose. The Android project is generated by `cordova platform add android` at build time (platforms/, gitignored), so there is no committed build.gradle, and T6 fails a declared module with none. The launcher label is written into config.xml <name> from .name by the engine instead.

upstream._doc: Full clone vendored as owned code (#253/#469: a clone, not a fork — no .git, no upstream remote, the submodule inlined). The brief said 'Acode is GPL — verify': it is NOT. license.txt at the pinned revision is MIT (Foxdebug / Ajit Kumar). The GPL in upstream's tree is the PREBUILT proot/talloc binaries and Alpine rootfs of src/plugins/proot, which are PRUNED here: they are GPL-2.0/LGPL binaries shipped without corresponding source, and the F-Droid flavour this fleet builds removes that plugin anyway. Full inventory in CLOUD-CODE.md. Guarded twice: test/test-cloud-nav.sh keeps every `pruned` path absent and refuses any *.so / *.rootfs in the tree, and the FLEET licence guard (1_cicd/src/data/licence-boundaries.json::upstreams.acode, run by licence-guard.yml on every push, #239) fails the repository if the plugin directory returns or package.json / package-lock.json / config.xml name it again.

flavor._doc: Upstream's own build axes (utils/scripts/build.sh): 'paid' = no AdMob plugin and no ads; 'fdroid' = no proot plugin and no Google Play Billing (cordova-plugin-iap). The engine reproduces exactly those two choices; nothing in the editor is patched to get there.

artifact_assert._doc: Read by cloud-code-engine.sh::_assert_apk_payload. gradle signs a perfectly valid APK around an empty www/, so the BUILT ARTIFACT must carry the web bundle AND this app's own layer: the nav module's marker string is looked for inside the shipped main.js, so an APK built from a tree that lost the seam fails here, not on the phone.

modules._doc: Shared gradle modules the Cordova-generated project includes BY REFERENCE. Cordova rewrites platforms/android/settings.gradle on every build and applies settings-extras.gradle from it; config.xml copies ours there, and it iterates this map, resolving each dir against THIS directory (the base the ship workflow's triggers and the publish gate resolve it against), never against the gradle root two levels down. build-extras.gradle links :libs:core into :app. libs:devtools finds this file by walking up from that gradle root.

libs:core._doc_dir: Fleet mesh membership (#743): core manifest-merges the CONSTELLATION_DATA signature permission (defined and requested). Declared so a core change rebuilds this app instead of shipping a stale mesh member.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Pulled in by core's `api project(':libs:devtools')` (FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, MESH_MEMBER <queries>); not linked directly. Listed so its changes also trigger a rebuild, and because Gradle resolves core's project path against this app's settings.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:text-tools._doc: The ITextTools binder (a `contract` lib): Profile & Config shows whether the fleet Account (Cloud Account) answers and whether it holds an OpenRouter key, through the key-free aiRoutingSnapshot (key_present, key_hint). The key itself is never read here (decisions-use guard D5: no new module holds it); the Chat pays with the token pasted in Profile & Config. Linked in build-extras.gradle.

modules._doc_ai: libs:ai is NOT a module here either (a Compose lib): its assets dir (assets/ai/ai.json, the shared AI contract nav.json::chat.ai points at, and protocol-cases.json) is compiled in by reference from build-extras.gradle, and tools/resolve-targets.py reads the same file at build time. nav.json restates no gateway and no OpenRouter endpoint.
modules._doc_model_catalogue: libs:model-catalogue is NOT a module here: it is a Compose lib and this Cordova app has no Compose, so build-extras.gradle compiles its logic package dir and its assets dir by reference (the libs/sysdns precedent); the lib closure counts it as a source input from that literal path.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1352 Configs ▸ General and ▸ About (fleetconfigs): FleetConfigsActivity, started from this app's own menu. Shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:bottomnav._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:ui-icons._doc: libs:bottomnav's dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:theme-background._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency (the page background); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:perms._doc: #1360/#1352 libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency: Configs ▸ General ▸ Perms is libs:perms' AppPermsSection, first run asks every never-asked grant.

ui._doc: #1158 the nav declaration the fleet's nav-shape guard reads (ui.bottom_nav, sections, default_section). Cloud Code is a Cordova WebView, so the bars are drawn in the page by src/cloud/bars-dom.js from src/cloud/nav.json (which stays the tab and sub-page source: the guard fails when the two disagree, rule W2). The shared Compose libs cannot be hosted in a Cordova page without a second window over the editor (see src/cloud/index.js); nav.json::bars carries the libs' sizes and colours and rule W3 holds them equal to the Kotlin constants. The first row is declared in nav.json::bars.first_row (not ui.top_bar: cloud-android-top-bar-guard holds the Compose AppTopBar; the nav-shape guard's rule W holds this one). AI hands over to the SuperApp (extapp:cloud-superapp/ai), Profile to Cloud Account (extapp:cloud-account), Configs opens Cloud Code's settings page.

web._doc: #876 Cloud Code as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-code-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-code-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: this app declares no bottom-nav island, so the page is one dense list of mock data. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

tests._doc: Shell testers under ac_cloud-code/test/, run by cloud-android-test-engine.sh shell in the ship workflow's FIRST step, before any toolchain. None needs a build.

cordova_surface._doc: Read by test/test-cordova-plugin-surface.sh — the Cordova form of #543's Capacitor trap. web_roots are walked to DERIVE every service name the bundle hands the bridge (cordova.exec(ok, err, 'Service', ...)); the registration side is DERIVED from package.json::cordova.plugins (what `cordova prepare` installs) minus upstream.flavor.removed_plugins, each mapped through package.json's file: dependency to its plugin.xml <feature name>. No service name is written in the tester.

_doc_fleet_agents: This app's agents, in the fleet agent registry's one shape (aa_cloud-superapp/build.json::_doc_fleet_agents). Consolidated into aa_cloud-superapp/data/fleet-agents.json by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-fleet-agents.py and shown in Cloud SuperApp ▸ Configs ▸ Apps ▸ Agents ▸ Fleet agents.

fleet_agents.trigger: on demand (a chat turn in Cloud Code Agents or Chat, or Cloud Search chat)

status.reason: live state is the gateway /health over the mesh (HTTP); the SuperApp does not call it

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.description: Cloud Code is the fleet's own signed build of Acode, the Android code editor, with a seven-tab bottom nav over it: the project backlog, the editor, the repositories, an AI chat, agent batches, a browser and a terminal. It exists so the owner can pick up a ticket, open the repository, change code, ask an agent and check the result from the phone, using the fleet's git proxy and AI gateway.
features: Backlog by status, project, priority and effort
Git through the fleet's git proxy

screens.name: Backlog
screens.what: Tickets by status, project, priority and effort.

guide: Open its repository in Repos and edit in Editor.
Ask the AI or start an agent batch for bigger changes.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.

related.why: Git status of the fleet's repositories.
Signs in to the fleet and holds the tokens and secrets this app reads.

about.credits: Upstream: Acode (github.com/Acode-Foundation/Acode), MIT licence, by Ajit Kumar and the Acode Foundation. Cloud Code vendors it as owned code and adds the backlog, repository, AI, agent, browser and terminal tabs.
